title: Rapid response battlecard - mini sales deck (WIP)
content:
Purpose: a compact, field-friendly battlecard + 6-slide mini deck for quick prep before customer calls. Designed for SDR/AE to move from discovery -> solution preference in a single 15–30 minute call.

Intended audience: AEs, SDRs, Solutions Engineers, AE Managers who need a short, repeatable play for common inference buyer archetypes (SaaS product teams, infra/platform teams, regulated enterprise).

High-level claim (30s elevator):
Redwood lets engineering teams run production LLM features with predictable latency and cost — from a hosted API for fast rollout to private/Dedicated deployments when control or SLAs matter. We help products ship faster and avoid expensive infra rebuilds.

How to use this doc:
- 1 min skim for AE: understand the decision ladder and 3 quick scripts.
- 5–10 min with SE: drill into performance numbers and rollout patterns.
- Use the snippets below verbatim when time is short.

Customer archetypes & primary value props (one line each):
- Product-led SaaS (rapid prototyping): Hosted API — speed to market, pay-as-you-go, sample rate limits.
- Mid-market with predictable growth: Dedicated — reserved GPU capacity + cost predictability.
- Regulated/finance/healthcare: Private — VPC or on-prem with KMS and audit logs.
- Platform/infra teams: Unified runtime & tooling — same APIs across environments, rollout and observability.

Decision ladder (quick checklist to qualify in discovery):
1) Who owns infra decisions? (product vs infra/platform)
2) Data sensitivity? (PII/regulatory -> Private)
3) Traffic profile: bursty spikes or predictable steady-state? (bursty -> hosted/dedicated burst; steady -> dedicated)
4) Latency SLOs (ms target) and percentile we need (p50/p95/p99)
5) Cost target per 1k tokens or per inference?
6) Existing tooling: require SSO, KMS, SIEM integrations?

Three quick scripts (engineer-friendly, procurement-friendly, executive-friendly):
- Engineer (40–60s): "We can try Redwood's hosted API in dev this afternoon — no infra changes. It gives you streaming responses, tool-calling and a model catalog tuned for low latency. If performance or data policies require it, we can plan a Dedicated or Private deployment later with identical APIs so your code doesn't change."
- Procurement (40–60s): "We offer usage-based billing for hosted scenarios and committed monthly capacity for Dedicated. Dedicated contracts can reduce unit cost by X–Y% depending on commit; we can model customer traffic in a quick cost exercise."
- Exec (30s): "Redwood reduces time-to-market for LLM features and avoids building a custom serving stack. We guarantee operational controls and fallback paths so customer-facing features stay live under traffic spikes."

Top 8 objection handlers (short):
1) "We host everything ourselves" -> A: "We integrate with existing infra and also offer Private deployments; many customers keep control while offloading runtime upkeep and kernel optimizations."
2) "Pricing unclear" -> A: "We’ll run a free pilot and model expected unit costs; our Optimize toolkit suggests batching/quantization to reduce expenses."
3) "Latency concerns" -> A: "Share your p95/p99 targets and a sample payload; we’ll run a quick benchmark against our hosted stack and Dedicated profiles."
4) "Model lock-in" -> A: "We support multiple open models and let customers pin versions; you can switch model variants with minimal code change."
5) "Security/compliance" -> A: "Private deployment, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and SOC/ISO artifacts available via enterprise pack."
6) "We need caching / dedup" -> A: "Automatic prefix caching and lightweight KV cache options in the runtime — we can show perf wins on your workload."
7) "Scaling surprises" -> A: "Smart routing and fallback policies keep traffic moving; Dedicated includes autoscaling and burst capacity options."
8) "Lack of observability" -> A: "Console gives token-level cost + latency breakdowns; SE can demo per-route tracing in 20 minutes."

Short competitive notes (talking points, not exhaustive):
- Compared to big cloud AI endpoints: Redwood emphasizes production-grade runtime optimizations, predictable unit economics, and consistent API across hosted/dedicated/private.
- Compared to self-hosted open-source runtimes: Redwood reduces ops surface (kernel selection, continuous batching, KV cache) and provides rollouts + SLO tooling out of the box.
- Comparative weakness to call out if asked: We are newer at some large-region coverage vs mega-clouds; highlight our enterprise region roadmap and Dedicated options.

Fast ROI math (script + template):
- Template variables: calls_per_day, avg_tokens_per_call, cost_hosted_per_1k_tokens (c_hosted), cost_dedicated_unit (c_dedicated), infra_ops_hours_saved_per_month (h_saved), engineer_hourly_rate (r)
- Example quick calc (say 100k calls/day, 200 tokens/call): tokens/day = 20M -> 20k * c_hosted per day. If Dedicated reduces unit cost by 30% at scale, show annual savings and subtract committed cost to show payback.
- Use SE to fill c_dedicated for specific model/quantization combos.

When to loop in SE / Solutions Eng (rules of thumb):
- Customer asks for p95 < 200ms or p99 < 500ms for >10k qps equivalent.
- Regulated data (PII/PHI) or need for VPC/on-prem.
- Wants a proof-of-performance: bring SE for a 2-hour benchmark with sample payloads.

Suggested 6-slide mini-deck outline (use for quick share after initial call):
1) Title + TL;DR (one sentence value + next step)
2) Customer problem we solve (3 bullets: latency, cost, operations) + 1 customer example
3) Our options mapped to buyer needs (hosted, dedicated, private) with one-sentence benefit each
4) Performance and reliability guarantees (typical numbers, burst/fallback story) + SE contact
5) Pricing model snapshot + sample ROI numbers (very small table)
6) Next steps: pilot proposal or SE benchmark checklist

Demo checklist for a 20-minute SE session (fast):
- Load sample prompts (we'll measure p50/p95/p99)
- Show streaming + function-calling in action
- Run a tiny Dedicated config benchmark if they have latency demands
- Walk Console: token costs, tracing, rollouts

Action items for AE after call:
- Send mini-deck + 2-sentence recap within 24h.
- Capture decision ladder answers in CRM (owner, data sensitivity, traffic, latency SLO, budget cadence).
- If SE required, book a 2-hour slot and collect sample payloads.

Open questions / to refine:
- Standardize the quick ROI numbers by model family (small, medium, large) — request input from Applied ML.
- Consolidate common benchmark payloads per vertical (search, summarization, codegen).

Notes to self (rough):
- Try replacing the generic ROI template with 1–2 anonymized customer examples next iteration.
- Add a one-pager for procurement: contract windows, standard discounts for Dedicated commits.

Footer:
